description_en: The Pinchẽ Gaṇeśa Temple located at Pinchẽ Ṭola is thesthānadeva(area deity) of the locality. It is also known as Jora (twin) Gaṇeśa, as two statues are enshrined together in the sanctum.Locals worship two aniconic stone statues inside the sanctum as Lord Gaṇeśa. It is a tradition that the residents of the Ṭola first worship this Gaṇeśa before performing any auspicious rituals at their household. This west-facing Temple has a three-tier roof of tiles with a finial of gilded copper. A parasol (chatra)is placed atop of the finial along with a flag of gilded copper. A banner (patāḥ)hangs from the pinnacle down to the eaves of the bottom roof. The main entrance that leads to the sanctum is covered by brass sheets. Atoraṇaalso covered by brass sheets is placed on top of the entrance, and a stone pillar erected in VS 2011 (1954 CE) with a statue of a mole on its top stands in front of the Temple.According to an oral tradition, there used to be bushes of nettle in the place where the Temple stands now. Two white elephants attained perfection or liberation (siddha juye) as they were eating nettle leaves and originated into two stones representing Lord Gaṇeśa at the same place. The tradition of worshipping the two stones as Gaṇeśa began then onwards.The shrine with two aniconic stones received minor renovations in NS 741 (1621 CE). A Temple was constructed only during the joint rule of King Siddhinarasiṃha and Śrīnivāsa Malla in NS 773 (1653 CE). The Temple received a golden finial hooded by a parasol in NS 818 (1698 CE). Historical records show that a golden crown was also offered to the deity in NS 825 (1705 CE), but it is not seen at present. The Temple went through a renovation in NS 857 (1737 CE) and a complete reconstruction took place in VS 2058 (2001 CE).The Temple has no priest and hence there is no separate caretakers (dyaḥpāḥlāḥ) here. Aguthiat Pinchẽ Ṭola associated with this Temple carries out the exhibition of a metal-sheet image of Gaṇeśa every year during the Indrajātrā (Yẽnyāḥ)festival in front of the main statues in the sanctum.Samaybajiis also distributed on this day.
description_ne: पिन्छेँ टोलमा रहेको गणेशको यस मन्दिरलाई पिन्छेँ टोलको थान गणेशको रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ । त्यसैले पिन्छेँ टोलमा कसैको पास्नी, व्रतबन्ध, भीमरथारोहण जस्ता संस्कार गर्दा सबैभन्दा पहिले यहीँ आएर पूजा गर्नुपर्ने परम्परा रहिआएको छ । पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यस मन्दिरमा तीन तहको झिंगटीका छानाहरू राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरमा धातुको गजूर राखिएको छ । गजूरमाथि छत्र चढाई धातुको झण्डा पनि राखिएको छ । गजूरदेखि मन्दिरको पहिलो तहको छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी धातुको पता: झुण्ड्याइएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोका र खापामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको छ । ढोकामाथि पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको तोरण राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र स्थापना गरिएको आकृतिविहीन दुईवटा ढुङ्गालाई गणेशको रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ । दुईजना गणेश स्थापना गरिएकोले यसलाई जोर गणेश पनि भनिन्छ । मन्दिर अगाडि विसं २०११ मा स्थापना गरिएको छुचुन्द्रो सहितको शिलास्तम्भ रहेको छ ।यस ठाउँमा पहिले सिस्नुको झार थियो । दुईजना सेता हात्तीहरू सिस्नु खाँदाखाँदै यसै ठाउँमा सिद्ध भएका थिए । ती हात्तीहरू सिद्ध भएको ठाउँमा गणेशको प्रतीकस्वरूप दुईवटा शिला उत्पन्न भएका थिए । ढुङ्गा मात्र भएको देवस्थलमा नेसं ७४१ (सन् १६२१) मा केही मर्मतको काम गरिएको थियो । पछि नेसं ७७३ (सन् १६५३) मा राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्ल र श्रीनिवास मल्लको संयुक्त शासनकालमा मात्र त्यस ठाउँमा मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको थियो । नेसं ८१८ (सन् १६९८) मा मन्दिरमा सुनको गजूर र छत्र चढाइएको थियो । नेसं ८२५ (सन् १७०५) मा गणेशलाई सुनको मुकुट चढाइएको थियो, तर अहिले सो मुकुट देखिँदैन । नेसं ८५७ (सन् १७३७) मा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो भने विसं २०५८ (सन् २००१) मा मन्दिरलाई जगैदेखि भत्काएर पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।मन्दिरमा कुनै पुजारी नियुक्त गरिएको छैन र कोही द्य:पा:ला: पनि बस्दैनन् । यो मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित पिन्छेँ टोलमा एउटा गुठी रहेको छ । त्यस गुठीले प्रत्येक वर्ष इन्द्रजात्राको दिनमा गर्भगृहमा रहेको गणेशको मूर्ति अगाडि धातुको पाताले बनेको गणेशको अर्को मूर्ति प्रदर्शन गर्ने परम्परा छ । त्यस दिन समयबजि पनि वितरण गरिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: As mentioned before, there was a small shrine in this place before it was replaced by a proper temple structure. The inscription records about a renovation of the shrine carried out by Jakerāma, Nugurāja, Dharamakesa and others.
The inscription cannot be deciphered because it is heavily eroded, thus its content remains obscure.

Before Halisaṅkhara (Hariśaṅkara), Satyāra, Abhayakesa Māhāna and other people jointly constructed a proper Temple during the joint rule of King Siddhinarasiṃha and Śrīnivāsa Malla, there was a small shrine in this place.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a golden pinnacle and umbrella
historical_events.event_description: Śivarāma Bhāro, Devarāma Bhāro, Jitalasiṃha Bhāvo and others jointly offered the pinnacle and umbrella to the Temple.
Bekvadala Bhāro and his wife Sivadevī offered the golden crown to Gaṇeśa.

historical_events.event_name: Repair of Temple with teliā bricks
historical_events.event_description: Madhanasimha Bhāvo repaired the Temple usingteliābricks.
Lakṣmisĩ Bhāvo and others constructed thecapāḥat Pinchẽ Ṭola.
Punasi, Sighavīra, Jogīlāla and Kṛsamā jointly covered thetoraṇawith brass sheets.
A group of twenty-four people including Dhijavigula and Jigidhaṃ offered the brasstoraṇakept atop of the door to the sanctum.
Saṅkharvi (Śaṅkaravīra) covered the door to the sanctum with brass sheets.
The Shrew Pillar (see the monument objects and site plan above) was installed in front of the Temple by Āsāmāna and Aṣṭamāyā. Statues of Āsāmāna and Aṣṭamāyā can be seen on the bottom of the Pillar.
Bhājumāna offered the new bell after the one offered in 1957 CE (NS 1077) was broken.

historical_events.event_name: Offering a pair of metal flags
historical_events.event_description: Nhuche Bāhādura and Machimāyā's sons and grandsons Gaṇeśa Bāhādura, Dineśa and Śrīgeśa jointed offered the pair of metal flags to Gaṇeśa.
The Temple was jointly reconstructed from the then Lalitpur Metropolitan City Office, Patan Conservation and Development Program (PCDP) and local residents.
Sānukājī Maharjan together with his family members offered the brasspatāḥto Gaṇeśa .
There is no trace of inscription on the stone tablet due to a heavy erosion and coverage by oily substances.
